question.problem:
Find $f(5)$ given that  $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are two continuous vector-valued functions for which   $g(5)=⟨-1,1,-2⟩$ and 

$$
{lim}_{t\to 5}[f(t)+3g(t)]=⟨1,3,1⟩\,.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Using the  addition rule for limits, and the fact that both functions are continuous, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 5}[f(t)+3g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 5}f(t)+{lim}_{t\to 5}[3g(t)] \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 5}f(t)+3{lim}_{t\to 5}g(t) \\  & =f(5)+3g(5) \\  & =f(5)+3{{⟨-1,1,-2⟩}_{⏟}}_{g(5)} \\  & =f(5)+⟨-3,3,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, we are told that

$$
{lim}_{t\to 5}[f(t)+3g(t)]=⟨1,3,1⟩.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain the following equation which we can solve for $f(5):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 5}[f(t)+3g(t)] & =⟨1,3,1⟩ \\ f(5)+⟨-3,3,-6⟩ & =⟨1,3,1⟩ \\ f(5) & =⟨1,3,1⟩-⟨-3,3,-6⟩ \\ f(5) & =⟨4,0,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$
